A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 18-page UltraDelta paper, including Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish identical substantive content, with differences confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original UltraDelta compression experiments across language, vision, and vision-language models, including component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the original compression evaluations and ablations, including the numerical results in Tables 1–5 and 7–10.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same variance-based sparsity allocation, distribution-aware compression, and trace-norm-guided rescaling procedures. The non-quantized variant in Appendix A is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LLM tasks, eight GLUE tasks, eight-task vision suite, 30-task ViT-B/16 suite, and three BEiT-3 vision-language tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain individual fine-tuned models, BitDelta, Delta-CoMe, DARE, and magnitude pruning. Traditional multitask learning remains in the vision comparisons, and DARE remains the DAC ablation comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain identical model configurations, evaluation metrics, quantization widths, sparsity settings, and testing procedures, including linear-layer-only compression and FP16 storage.

E4.justification: The component ablation, DAC comparison across 30 tasks, quantization and sparsity-step analyses, trace-norm analysis, and embedding-similarity analysis are unchanged in Figures 3–6 and Tables 5, 9, and 10.

E5.justification: Point-estimate reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted results are identical. For example, UltraDelta retains a T5-base average of 86.74 at 800× compression in Table 2 and a ViT-B/32 average of 90.7 at 133× in Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are unchanged, including the Gaussian entropy–variance relationship and activation-error derivations in Section 3.3 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about a data-free pipeline combining ultra-high compression with strong performance, its three components, and effectiveness across model families.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same regularization explanation, interpretation of compression differences through model redundancy, and limitation concerning heuristic trace-norm-based rescaling.

D1.justification: Checkpoint IDs in Table 6, the single NVIDIA A800 hardware disclosure, compression hyperparameters, and implementation and overhead discussion are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 75 references are identical. The positioning relative to earlier pruning, quantization, and hybrid compression methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 19 May 2025 to v2 dated 19 Jun 2025. All manuscript prose, terminology, headings, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The vertical arXiv stamp on page 1 is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–10, and all substantive page layouts are unchanged; pages 2–18 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, results, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are unchanged. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful difference in scientific support, clarity, reproducibility, or overall paper quality.
